title: S. aureus sortase A ΔN59: why P94 substitutions raise activity and whether the β7-β8 loop is involved
objective: Find out whether P94 substitutions raise sortase A activity by releasing the closed β7-β8 loop (through Y187/W194 contact), through the chemistry of the introduced residue, or through a route independent of the loop, using one precisely edited ΔN59 core and matched controls.
coordinate_note: All coordinates are construct positions: residues 60-206 of UniProt Q2FV99 are positions 1-147, so native (full-length) number = construct position + 59 (P94 is position 35, Y187 position 128). Prose, site labels and the literature use native numbers.

regions.name: Ca2+ site (beta3-beta4 loop)
regions.description: Acidic pocket that binds the allosteric Ca2+ ion; Ca2+ raises wild-type activity roughly eight-fold, mainly by lowering KM.

regions.name: Helix H1 N-terminal turn
regions.description: T93 (N-cap) and the first turn of helix H1, with P94 at its first helical position. Boundaries assigned here from backbone dihedrals of 1T2P, 1IJA and 2KID.

regions.name: Beta4/H2 loop (catalytic His side)
regions.description: Loop carrying the general acid/base His120; D124G in this loop was reported to raise activity of the evolved enzyme. Boundaries assigned here.

regions.name: Beta6-beta7 loop
regions.description: Loop that closes over the LPXTG leucine/proline pocket on substrate binding (3-10 helix V166-L169 forms in the complex) and holds a Ca2+ ligand (E171). Boundaries assigned here and approximate.

regions.name: Beta7-beta8 loop
regions.description: Loop between catalytic C184 and R197 that lies against the substrate groove and is displaced about 8-13 angstroms when the sorting signal is attached.

hypotheses.question: Is loss of the proline ring's packing against the closed β7-β8 loop enough to raise activity, whatever replaces it?
hypotheses.mechanism: In apo and closed-loop structures the P94 ring is 3-4 Å from Y187 and W194; in the substrate-attached NMR complex it is more than 10 Å from both. Alanine removes the ring's contact surface and adds no charge or polarity, so a gain from P94A would point to released packing as sufficient.
hypotheses.measurement: kcat, KM(LPETG), KM(Gly3) and kcat/KM by HPLC (Abz-LPETGK(Dnp) with GGG-COOH) for the reference, P94A and P94S, with and without 10 mM CaCl2. Thermal stability (DSF) and soluble yield alongside, so activity is not read from unstable or poorly expressed protein.
hypotheses.note: P94A keeps Cβ, which is also within contact distance, so a partial effect would not separate partial release from backbone effects.

hypotheses.question: Does the charge of the introduced residue add to or subtract from the ring-removal effect?
hypotheses.mechanism: A charged residue at 94 could act on loop residues near D186, E189 and K190 or on the helix dipole at the H1 start, rather than only by removing the ring. P94D (acidic) and P94R (basic, the evolved residue) have opposite charge; if both match P94A the sign of the charge is not what matters.
hypotheses.measurement: Same kinetic panel for P94D and P94R against P94A and P94S; the question is whether activity orders by ring removal (all similar) or by charge (D and R differ).
hypotheses.note: P94R is reported only inside the pentamutant before 2026 in the sources examined, so its single-mutant effect is a gap this construct fills.

hypotheses.question: Does the P94 gain depend on Y187 in the β7-β8 loop?
hypotheses.mechanism: If P94 substitutions act by releasing a contact with Y187, removing the Y187 side chain should itself raise activity and make P94S non-additive: the double mutant should be about as active as the better single. If P94S acts through a separate route the double should be close to the product of the two single effects.
hypotheses.measurement: Two-by-two comparison of reference, P94S, Y187A and P94S/Y187A on log(kcat/KM) and log KM(LPETG); the interaction term is the readout. Backbone-sensitive reporters (W194 indole N-H in 15N-HSQC) can show whether the loop state changes in each cell.
hypotheses.note: Pentamutant data show Y187 effects depend on E189 (Y187L/E189R up, Y187R/E189K down), so Y187A may do more than release P94.

hypotheses.question: Is the P94 contribution still present once the other loop mutations of the evolved enzyme are in place?
hypotheses.mechanism: K190E and K196T lie in the β7-β8 loop and D160N/D165A in the β6-β7 region. If those four already open the loop, restoring or removing P94R should matter little (sub-additive); if P94 acts by a separate route, P94R should add about its wild-type-background effect, as the largely additive single-mutant effects reported for the selection suggest.
hypotheses.measurement: Compare the P94 to R94 step in the wild-type background (reference vs P94R) with the same step in the four-mutant background (4M-P94 vs pentamutant), as a ratio of kcat/KM and of KM(LPETG), with and without Ca2+ (pentamutant activity is Ca2+-dependent).
hypotheses.note: The four-mutant enzyme with native P94 has not been described in the sources examined, and the D160N/D165A/K190E/K196T set may be unstable without P94R.

sites.label: P94 — substitutions raise activity

observations.finding: P94S and P94R were both recovered repeatedly from yeast-display selections; P94 lies at the N terminus of helix 1. Single substitutions raised kcat/KM about 2-4-fold over wild type (P94S 600 vs 200 M-1 s-1), and single-mutant effects were described as largely additive.
observations.context: Wild-type S. aureus SrtA, yeast display then solution kinetics with an LPETG substrate and Gly3 nucleophile at 22.5 C; construct boundary not stated in the paper.

observations.finding: A variant selected by DHFR protein-complementation carries P94H, and P94 is the only position mutated in both that selection and the Chen pentamutant; the two substitutions are both basic. DEER distances from K67 to K190 or K196 lengthen by about 10 Å with substrate present, consistent with scissor-like β7-β8 loop opening.
observations.context: SrtA ΔN59 core (residues 60-206), error-prone PCR then complementation selection; spin-labelled DEER on a Cys-free C184A background.

sites.note: First residue of helix H1. Observed as S and R in yeast-display selections and as H in a complementation selection; no pre-2026 source examined here characterises single P94R, P94A or P94D in a wild-type background. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: P94 packs on Y187 and W194 in closed-loop structures

observations.finding: Analysis of the deposited apo NMR ensemble (SrtA residues 60-206) places the P94 side chain within 4.5 Å of Y187 in 19 of 25 models and of W194 in 23 of 25; T93 Cα to K190 Cα averages 15.3 Å (14.8-16.3).
observations.context: Heavy-atom distance analysis of PDB 1IJA in this study, not a statement made in the source paper. Same ΔN59 construct as proposed.

observations.finding: In the apo crystal structure (1T2P chain A) the P94 side chain is 3.4 Å from Y187 and 3.9 Å from W194; the LPETG complex crystal (1T2W, catalytic Cys replaced) keeps the same contacts (3.4 and 4.0 Å).
observations.context: Heavy-atom distance analysis in this study, not a statement made in the source paper. The 1T2W complex has a closed-type β7-β8 loop and a different β6-β7 loop from the NMR complex.

observations.finding: In the substrate-attached NMR complex the P94 side chain is 13.9 Å from Y187 and 10.7 Å from W194, and T93 Cα to K190 Cα lengthens to 23.5 Å (23.1-23.9), against 15.3 Å in the apo ensemble. The paper itself reports the 7/8 loop displaced about 13 Å on substrate attachment, with the loop's C-terminal end next to the N-terminal end of helix H1 in the crystal but separate in the NMR complex.
observations.context: Solution NMR of SrtA with a covalently attached LPAT analogue; distances computed here from the deposited 20-model ensemble.

sites.note: Contact geometry is read from deposited structures; that this contact limits activity is a hypothesis, not a measurement. The closed-loop 1T2W crystal complex keeps the contact, so contact loss tracks loop opening rather than substrate occupancy alone. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: T93 — probable N-cap of helix H1
sites.note: Inferred here: T93 Oγ1 is 3.3 Å from the backbone N of residue 96 in 1T2P (3.9 Å in 1IJA model 1), the usual N-cap geometry. No source tests it. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: Y187 and E189 — loop residues whose changes improved the evolved enzyme

observations.finding: Saturation mutagenesis of Y187 and E189 on the pentamutant gave Y187L/E189R (about 3.2-fold above pentamutant kcat/KM, 11,425 vs 3,622 M-1 s-1), Y187L/E189A (1.1-fold) and Y187R/E189K (0.5-fold); the effects depend on the E189 partner as well as Y187.
observations.context: Pentamutant background (already carries P94R), HPLC kinetics with Abz-LPETGK(Dnp) and GGG; wild-type Y187 single mutants were not tested.

observations.finding: The thesis proposes that Y187 contacts P94 to hold the β7-β8 loop closed, that a charged residue at 94 would open it, and that Ca2+ opens the loop allosterically; the abstract page gives no activity values.
observations.context: WT, pentamutant and P94D saSrtA by 15N-HSQC and a FRET reporter; thesis, not peer reviewed; PDF not retrieved.

sites.note: Measured on the pentamutant, not on wild type. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: W194 — substrate-groove gatekeeper in the loop

observations.finding: The substrate threonine methyl packs beneath the W194 indole in the NMR complex, and this wedge is associated with the shift of the 7/8 loop.
observations.context: NMR complex with covalently attached LPAT analogue.

observations.finding: Seven W194 single mutants (A, D, F, G, N, S, Y) of saSrtA retained the LPXTG requirement for cleavage but changed nucleophile specificity, with W194A and W194S accepting a D-Ala nucleophile.
observations.context: FRET-based activity assay on purified saSrtA; abstract only.

observations.finding: Swapping the S. pneumoniae β7-β8 loop into saSrtA gave an inactive enzyme, while the saSrtA loop in S. pneumoniae SrtA reproduced saSrtA-like Gly-only selectivity; W194A in that chimera lowered LPATG conversion by 17% and admitted Ala and Ser at P1'.
observations.context: FRET assay with Abz-LPATXG-K(Dnp) peptides, 5 µM enzyme, 2 h.

sites.note: Its roles in P1' selectivity make W194 a poor choice for a clean P94 contact test. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: H120, C184, R197 — catalytic triad

observations.finding: The NMR structure places catalytic C184 where H120 can ionise it, and notes that Ca2+ binding near the active site stimulates catalysis, possibly by changing the conformation of a surface loop.
observations.context: Solution NMR of SrtA residues 60-206.

sites.note: Left unchanged in every construct. C184 and R197 flank the β7-β8 loop. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: E105, E108, E171 — Ca2+ ligands

observations.finding: Ca2+ raises wild-type activity about 8-fold by lowering KM, is placed between E105, E108 and E171, and slows β6-β7 loop motions.
observations.context: NMR relaxation and activity assays on SrtA residues 60-206.

observations.finding: Pentamutant-based variants were active only with 10 mM CaCl2, whereas adding E105K/E108Q conferred Ca2+ independence at the cost of lower activity without Ca2+.
observations.context: SrtA numbered on the full-length sequence; construct boundary not stated.

observations.finding: In MD the β7-β8 loop stays closed in apo SrtA and opens in the signal-bound state; Ca2+ sits in a pocket of E105, E108, D112 and N114. Helix H1, P94, Y187 and W194 are not discussed.
observations.context: 100-ns conventional and 40-ns accelerated MD from 1T2P (apo) and 2KID (holo).

sites.note: Unchanged in the library; Ca2+ is varied in the assay instead. E105K/E108Q is the published route to Ca2+ independence. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: D160 and K196 — loop-to-β6 contact

observations.finding: In saSrtA, K196 (β7-β8 loop, just before the catalytic R197) contacts D160; this loop-to-β6 contact was found to hinder activity in the sortase family and K196T/D160N are part of the evolved pentamutant. The β7-β8 loop spans the catalytic C184 to R197 in saSrtA.
observations.context: Structure-based analysis and mutants of S. pneumoniae SrtA plus chimeras; the saSrtA assignments are inferred from structure, not tested by saSrtA mutagenesis in that paper.

observations.finding: D160 and D165 sit in the region joining β6 and β7; D165 begins the 3-10 helix that forms on LPAT binding and contacts the substrate leucine; K196 is at the C-terminal end of the β7-β8 loop. K190E was enriched in the selection without a structural location being given.
observations.context: Mapping of selected mutations onto the wild-type SrtA-LPAT solution structure.

sites.note: Both positions are mutated in the evolved pentamutant (D160N, K196T). The pairing is inferred from structure. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: D165 and K190 — other pentamutant positions

observations.finding: D160 and D165 sit in the region joining β6 and β7; D165 begins the 3-10 helix that forms on LPAT binding and contacts the substrate leucine; K196 is at the C-terminal end of the β7-β8 loop. K190E was enriched in the selection without a structural location being given.
observations.context: Mapping of selected mutations onto the wild-type SrtA-LPAT solution structure.

observations.finding: The P94R/D160N/D165A/K190E/K196T pentamutant reached about 120-fold higher kcat/KM than wild type (23,000 vs 200 M-1 s-1), mostly through lower KM for LPETG (7.6 to 0.23 mM) with a 3.6-fold higher kcat; KM for Gly3 rose about 20-fold.
observations.context: Solution kinetics, LPETG substrate and Gly3 nucleophile, 22.5 C.

sites.note: D165 is at the start of the 3-10 helix that forms with substrate; K190 is in the β7-β8 loop. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

sites.label: D124 — β4/H2 loop residue near H120

observations.finding: D124G (β4/H2 loop, near H120) was found by random mutagenesis, raised wild-type activity about 3-fold, and was roughly additive on the pentamutant; D186G in the β7-β8 loop lowered pentamutant activity.
observations.context: HPLC kinetics, wild-type and pentamutant backgrounds.

sites.note: Not edited here. Native (full-length) numbering is construct position + 59; all literature numbers are native.

variants.name: SrtA ΔN59 reference
variants.headline: Wild-type ΔN59 core
variants.note: Residues 60-206 of UniProt Q2FV99 (S. aureus NCTC 8325 SrtA), 147 aa, no tag and no added Met in the record; add the same vector tag and start codon context to every construct.

variants.name: P94A
variants.headline: Alanine at the helix H1 start

rationale.hypothesis: Tests whether removing the proline ring, with no new charge or polarity, is enough to raise activity.

observations.finding: Analysis of the deposited apo NMR ensemble (SrtA residues 60-206) places the P94 side chain within 4.5 Å of Y187 in 19 of 25 models and of W194 in 23 of 25; T93 Cα to K190 Cα averages 15.3 Å (14.8-16.3).
observations.context: Heavy-atom distance analysis of PDB 1IJA in this study, not a statement made in the source paper. Same ΔN59 construct as proposed.

observations.finding: In the substrate-attached NMR complex the P94 side chain is 13.9 Å from Y187 and 10.7 Å from W194, and T93 Cα to K190 Cα lengthens to 23.5 Å (23.1-23.9), against 15.3 Å in the apo ensemble. The paper itself reports the 7/8 loop displaced about 13 Å on substrate attachment, with the loop's C-terminal end next to the N-terminal end of helix H1 in the crystal but separate in the NMR complex.
observations.context: Solution NMR of SrtA with a covalently attached LPAT analogue; distances computed here from the deposited 20-model ensemble.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference it shows the size of a pure ring-removal effect; against P94S, P94D and P94R it shows whether any introduced chemistry adds to it.
rationale.uncertainty: Ala keeps Cβ within contact distance of Y187, and loss of the proline's backbone constraint at the first helical position may change helix capping independently of the loop. A wild-type-like result would not exclude a loop contribution.
rationale.edit: Removes the ring that packs against Y187 and W194 in closed-loop structures and leaves a small neutral residue.
rationale.inference: Transfer assumption: the P94–Y187/W194 contact seen in apo and crystal coordinates is present in solution in the apo enzyme; that is supported by 19/25 and 23/25 NMR models but not tested by mutation in the sources examined.

variants.name: P94S
variants.headline: Serine at the helix H1 start

rationale.hypothesis: Benchmark substitution with published kinetics, giving the effect size against which P94A is read.

observations.finding: P94S and P94R were both recovered repeatedly from yeast-display selections; P94 lies at the N terminus of helix 1. Single substitutions raised kcat/KM about 2-4-fold over wild type (P94S 600 vs 200 M-1 s-1), and single-mutant effects were described as largely additive.
observations.context: Wild-type S. aureus SrtA, yeast display then solution kinetics with an LPETG substrate and Gly3 nucleophile at 22.5 C; construct boundary not stated in the paper.

observations.finding: P94S/D160N/K196T gave 8,600 M-1 s-1 versus 600, 600 and 400 for the three singles, about 2.4-fold above the product of the single-mutant effects.
observations.context: Solution kinetics as above; combination slightly super-additive for this triple.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference it reproduces the roughly 3-fold gain reported in the selection; against P94A it separates ring removal from an added hydroxyl that suits a helix N-terminal position.
rationale.uncertainty: The published single-mutant value (600 vs 200 M-1 s-1) comes from a different construct boundary, temperature series and assay, so it is a guide to the expected size, not a replacement for running the reference alongside.
rationale.edit: Replaces the ring with a small polar residue common at the first turn of a helix.

variants.name: P94D
variants.headline: Aspartate at the helix H1 start

rationale.hypothesis: Tests whether an acidic residue at 94 acts through charge, on loop residues or the helix dipole, beyond ring removal.

observations.finding: The thesis proposes that Y187 contacts P94 to hold the β7-β8 loop closed, that a charged residue at 94 would open it, and that Ca2+ opens the loop allosterically; the abstract page gives no activity values.
observations.context: WT, pentamutant and P94D saSrtA by 15N-HSQC and a FRET reporter; thesis, not peer reviewed; PDF not retrieved.

observations.finding: A variant selected by DHFR protein-complementation carries P94H, and P94 is the only position mutated in both that selection and the Chen pentamutant; the two substitutions are both basic. DEER distances from K67 to K190 or K196 lengthen by about 10 Å with substrate present, consistent with scissor-like β7-β8 loop opening.
observations.context: SrtA ΔN59 core (residues 60-206), error-prone PCR then complementation selection; spin-labelled DEER on a Cys-free C184A background.

rationale.comparison: Against P94A it isolates the effect of a negative charge; against P94R it reverses the charge while removing the same ring.
rationale.uncertainty: The only source proposing P94D here is an unreviewed thesis whose data were not seen. Asp at the first helical position also favours helix capping, so a gain would not by itself prove an electrostatic mechanism with the loop.
rationale.edit: Replaces the ring with a carboxylate that could face the acidic loop residues D186 and E189.
rationale.inference: Transfer assumption: the loop carries net negative charge near the P94 site (D186, E189) so that P94D would be repelled and P94R attracted; this was not tested.

variants.name: P94R
variants.headline: Arginine at the helix H1 start

rationale.hypothesis: Places the evolved residue in a wild-type background to give a single-mutant value for the substitution used in the pentamutant.

observations.finding: The P94R/D160N/D165A/K190E/K196T pentamutant reached about 120-fold higher kcat/KM than wild type (23,000 vs 200 M-1 s-1), mostly through lower KM for LPETG (7.6 to 0.23 mM) with a 3.6-fold higher kcat; KM for Gly3 rose about 20-fold.
observations.context: Solution kinetics, LPETG substrate and Gly3 nucleophile, 22.5 C.

observations.finding: A variant selected by DHFR protein-complementation carries P94H, and P94 is the only position mutated in both that selection and the Chen pentamutant; the two substitutions are both basic. DEER distances from K67 to K190 or K196 lengthen by about 10 Å with substrate present, consistent with scissor-like β7-β8 loop opening.
observations.context: SrtA ΔN59 core (residues 60-206), error-prone PCR then complementation selection; spin-labelled DEER on a Cys-free C184A background.

rationale.comparison: Against P94D it reverses the charge on the same site; against the reference and against the pentamutant it gives the P94R step in both backgrounds for the background hypothesis.
rationale.uncertainty: P94R was selected in a background that already carried D160N and later D165A, K196T and K190E, and there is no value for it alone in the sources examined, so its single-mutant effect may be small or may need those partners.
rationale.edit: Replaces the ring with the guanidinium residue found in the pentamutant.

variants.name: Y187A
variants.headline: Alanine in place of the loop's P94-contacting tyrosine

rationale.hypothesis: Removes the loop-side partner of the P94 contact to ask whether the loop alone, without any P94 change, can raise activity.

observations.finding: Saturation mutagenesis of Y187 and E189 on the pentamutant gave Y187L/E189R (about 3.2-fold above pentamutant kcat/KM, 11,425 vs 3,622 M-1 s-1), Y187L/E189A (1.1-fold) and Y187R/E189K (0.5-fold); the effects depend on the E189 partner as well as Y187.
observations.context: Pentamutant background (already carries P94R), HPLC kinetics with Abz-LPETGK(Dnp) and GGG; wild-type Y187 single mutants were not tested.

observations.finding: The thesis proposes that Y187 contacts P94 to hold the β7-β8 loop closed, that a charged residue at 94 would open it, and that Ca2+ opens the loop allosterically; the abstract page gives no activity values.
observations.context: WT, pentamutant and P94D saSrtA by 15N-HSQC and a FRET reporter; thesis, not peer reviewed; PDF not retrieved.

observations.finding: Analysis of the deposited apo NMR ensemble (SrtA residues 60-206) places the P94 side chain within 4.5 Å of Y187 in 19 of 25 models and of W194 in 23 of 25; T93 Cα to K190 Cα averages 15.3 Å (14.8-16.3).
observations.context: Heavy-atom distance analysis of PDB 1IJA in this study, not a statement made in the source paper. Same ΔN59 construct as proposed.

rationale.comparison: Against the reference it shows what releasing the contact from the loop side does; against P94S and the double mutant it gives the two singles needed for the interaction term.
rationale.uncertainty: Y187 sits in a loop that also hosts W194 and the E189 partner, so Y187A may change loop stability or substrate access without any link to P94. Pentamutant data show the sign of a Y187 change depends on E189. A drop in activity or stability would be uninformative about P94.
rationale.edit: Truncates the tyrosine side chain that lies against P94 in closed-loop structures.
rationale.inference: Transfer assumption: Y187 effects measured on the pentamutant (where P94 is already Arg) carry over to a wild-type background; they were not measured there.

rationale.hypothesis: Completes the two-by-two so the interaction between the P94 and Y187 changes can be read from the data.

observations.context: Wild-type S. aureus SrtA, yeast display then solution kinetics with an LPETG substrate and Gly3 nucleophile at 22.5 C; construct boundary not stated in the paper.

observations.context: Pentamutant background (already carries P94R), HPLC kinetics with Abz-LPETGK(Dnp) and GGG; wild-type Y187 single mutants were not tested.

rationale.comparison: Against P94S and Y187A it shows whether the two changes are additive in log activity (independent routes) or whether the double is no better than the stronger single (shared route).
rationale.uncertainty: If the double destabilises the enzyme, loss of activity could be misread as epistasis; compare with thermal stability and expression, and read the result only where the double is well folded.
rationale.edit: Combines the two substitutions of the singles in one molecule.

observations.finding: The P94R/D160N/D165A/K190E/K196T pentamutant reached about 120-fold higher kcat/KM than wild type (23,000 vs 200 M-1 s-1), mostly through lower KM for LPETG (7.6 to 0.23 mM) with a 3.6-fold higher kcat; KM for Gly3 rose about 20-fold.
observations.context: Solution kinetics, LPETG substrate and Gly3 nucleophile, 22.5 C.

observations.finding: In saSrtA, K196 (β7-β8 loop, just before the catalytic R197) contacts D160; this loop-to-β6 contact was found to hinder activity in the sortase family and K196T/D160N are part of the evolved pentamutant. The β7-β8 loop spans the catalytic C184 to R197 in saSrtA.
observations.context: Structure-based analysis and mutants of S. pneumoniae SrtA plus chimeras; the saSrtA assignments are inferred from structure, not tested by saSrtA mutagenesis in that paper.

observations.finding: D160 and D165 sit in the region joining β6 and β7; D165 begins the 3-10 helix that forms on LPAT binding and contacts the substrate leucine; K196 is at the C-terminal end of the β7-β8 loop. K190E was enriched in the selection without a structural location being given.
observations.context: Mapping of selected mutations onto the wild-type SrtA-LPAT solution structure.

observations.finding: Pentamutant-based variants were active only with 10 mM CaCl2, whereas adding E105K/E108Q conferred Ca2+ independence at the cost of lower activity without Ca2+.
observations.context: SrtA numbered on the full-length sequence; construct boundary not stated.

rationale.comparison: Against the pentamutant it differs only at position 94 (Pro versus Arg); against the reference it shows what the other four changes give without P94R.
rationale.uncertainty: This four-mutant set has not been reported with native P94 in the sources examined and may fold or express poorly. It changes four positions at once relative to the reference, so it is read only through its comparison with the pentamutant.
rationale.edit: Carries the four non-P94 substitutions of the evolved enzyme, two of them in the β7-β8 loop.
rationale.inference: Transfer assumption: the four substitutions act on the loop and groove independently of residue 94, as the largely additive single-mutant effects in the selection suggest.

rationale.hypothesis: Provides the widely used evolved enzyme as the comparator for the proline-restored four-mutant and as the activity benchmark.

precedent_search.scope: Web, PubMed Central, Europe PMC and bioRxiv searches for P94 substitutions, β7-β8 and β6-β7 loop mutants, Ca2+ activation, evolved SrtA variants and forward citations of the Chen 2011 and Johnson 2022 papers, limited to work dated before 2026-01-01 as requested. Search engines also returned items dated 2026 that address P94 variants directly; they were excluded from evidence and design here, so their results may overlap with or contradict constructs proposed in this library and should be read before building.

scale.higher_means: more conserved across this comparison set

method.homolog_source: UniRef50_Q2FV99 UniProtKB members (67 sequences), retrieved 2026-11-16; scored against residues 60-206
method.comparison_set: UniProtKB members of UniRef50_Q2FV99, the UniRef50 cluster containing Q2FV99: the same protein in other species, clustered by UniProt at 50% identity with an 80% length-overlap requirement. ORTHOLOG level: scores answer what this protein needs.
method.alignment: multiple alignment by FAMSA via pyfamsa 0.7.0, projected onto reference coordinates by dropping columns where the reference is gapped. It can score positions that MAFFT leaves unscored, with weak support, so read per-position coverage alongside the score
method.weighting: Henikoff position-based sequence weights, computed over variable columns only
method.effective_sequences_definition: Neff = sum(1/n_i), n_i counting sequences at least 80% identical to sequence i over positions where both have a residue (itself included); pairs overlapping less than 50% of the reference are not counted as similar. Reported unnormalised and divided by reference length; normalisation is not standardised in the literature, so compare only against values computed the same way. This is NOT the sum of the Henikoff weights, which is rescaled to the sequence count by construction and therefore always equals it.
method.score: Jensen-Shannon divergence against Robinson & Robinson background, scaled by column occupancy (Capra & Singh 2007)
